scam.title: Protect yourself from scams
scam.lead: People run scams in the name of the lottery. Know the official fee and check every step yourself.
scam.banner: Registering for the lottery has an official fee of just one dollar ($1), set by the US State Department. Any extra money is the office's service charge.

facts.1: You can register yourself on the official site that the US State Department announces.
facts.2: If you use an office, make sure it registers on the official site only, and that you personally keep the confirmation number.
facts.3: Nobody can guarantee a win or raise your chances.
facts.4: You check the result yourself, only on the official result page (Entrant Status Check). No email or message tells you that you won.
facts.5: Copycat sites look official. Make sure the address ends in .gov, and beware of anyone who asks for money to "win".

signs.1: Asks for money to "guarantee" a win or raise your chances.
signs.2: Tells you that you won by message, email or phone.
signs.3: Asks for a money transfer, card details or your passport before you check the official site.
signs.4: The address does not end in .gov, or the tone is urgent and threatening.

links.fee: The official decision on the registration fee (in the US official gazette, the Federal Register)

scam.note: This site is not affiliated with the US government. We only point you to the official pages.
scam.fee: Registering for the lottery has an official fee of just one dollar ($1), set by the US State Department. Do not let anyone take more than that as the government fee; any extra money is the office's service charge.

guide.title: How do I find the price of food and groceries?
guide.lead: We will not give you a number. We show you where to see it yourself, in the city you plan to live in.
guide.step1: Open a supermarket site from the links below and pick a store in your intended city.
guide.step2: Build a one-week basket of what you actually buy and read the total.
guide.step3: Multiply by 4 (the weeks in a month) and type the number into the calculator. Repeat now and then; prices change.
guide.note: These are external sites. We do not set prices and are not responsible for them.
guide.backToCalculator: Type the number into the calculator
guide.titleFor: How do I find the price of “{item}”?
guide.genericLead: We will not give you a number. We show you where to look, and you type the number into the calculator.
guide.genericStep1: Open the links below and look for the current fee or price.
guide.genericStep2: Type the number as you find it. Mind the currency, and whether it is one-off or monthly.
guide.genericStep3: Go back to the calculator and type the number. Check it now and then; prices and fees change.

guideHealth.title: How do I find the price of health insurance?
guideHealth.lead: We will not give you a number. The price depends on the state, your age, household size and income, and you see it yourself on the official US government site.
guideHealth.step1: Open the government health insurance site (HealthCare.gov), enter the ZIP code (postal code) of your intended city, and your household members and ages.
guideHealth.step2: Browse the plans and the monthly premium of each plan (the premium is what you pay the insurer every month).
guideHealth.step3: Type the monthly premium into the calculator. If you have children, include them in the household size so the premium covers them.
guideHealth.state: Some states run their own marketplace; HealthCare.gov sends you there automatically. We do not set prices.
guideHealth.subsidyWarning: HealthCare.gov may offer you a subsidy on the premium based on your income. As a new immigrant, do not take this subsidy; work out the full price without it.
guideHealth.subsidyWarningLink: Read the “public charge” page (not becoming a burden on the government)

itemIncludes.entryPhotos: Taking the photos the registration needs. You pay before registering and it does not come back. For each person on the entry: you, your spouse and the children.
itemIncludes.entryHelp: A fee for any office or person who fills in the registration for you, if you use one. You pay it at registration and it does not come back. For the whole family.
itemIncludes.familyPassports: Getting the passports of your spouse and children (not yours). You pay before the interview and it does not come back. For each family member.
itemIncludes.medicalExam: The examination, X-ray, blood test and vaccinations at the embassy's doctor. You pay the doctor before the interview and it does not come back. For each adult and anyone 15 or older. X-rays and blood tests start at 15.
itemIncludes.translation: A certified translator's fee and any stamp or attestation on documents, if you need it. You pay before the interview and it does not come back. For the whole family.
itemIncludes.civilCertificates: Getting new originals of the birth certificates, the marriage certificate, the degree and the transcript. You pay before the interview and it does not come back. For the whole family.
itemIncludes.militaryCertificate: The fee to get the military status or exemption certificate (for men). You pay before the interview and it does not come back. Type the total for the family if more than one person needs it.
itemIncludes.visaPhotos: The printed photos each person brings to the interview. These are separate from the registration photos. You pay before the interview and it does not come back. For each person.
itemIncludes.interviewTravel: Transport, a night's stay and meals around the interview, if you live outside Cairo. You pay around the interview day and it does not come back. For the whole family.
itemIncludes.passportCourier: Sending the passport back to an Aramex office you choose after the interview: free at the Cairo embassy. Type an amount only if your embassy charges. For each person.
itemIncludes.otherPaperwork: Any paperwork or fee before travel that has no box above. You pay it before you travel and it does not come back. Type the total for the whole family.
itemIncludes.travelInsurance: Trip and medical cover for the first weeks, before your health insurance starts. You pay before you travel and it does not come back. Choose "one person" or "the whole family" above.
itemIncludes.temporaryStay: A hotel or a furnished short stay until you move into your rented flat. You pay in the first days after you arrive and it does not come back. For the whole family.
itemIncludes.applicationFees: The fee to apply for a flat and for the background and credit check. You pay when you apply and it does not come back. For the whole family.
itemIncludes.securityDeposit: A sum you pay the landlord with the first rent. It comes back when you leave the flat if nothing is damaged. This is a rental, not a purchase, and not health or car insurance. For the whole flat.
itemIncludes.furniture: Beds, a sofa, a table, a TV and any large appliances. You buy them in the first month and the money does not come back. For the whole family.
itemIncludes.winterClothes: Coats, boots and warm clothes. You buy them in the first month and the money does not come back. For each person.
itemIncludes.householdBasics: Kitchen items, bed linen and blankets, cleaning and bathroom supplies. You buy them when you arrive and the money does not come back. For the whole family. Food is not here: it is in the monthly costs.
itemIncludes.utilityDeposits: A sum utility companies sometimes ask for when you open a new account with no credit history. You pay when you open the account. Ask the company whether it comes back. For the whole flat.
itemIncludes.phoneLine: A SIM and activating the line for the first time. You pay in the first month and it does not come back. For each adult. The monthly plan is in the monthly costs.
itemIncludes.licenseTests: Test fees and getting the driving licence. You pay in the first months and it does not come back. For adults only.
itemIncludes.carPurchase: The price of the car only. You pay when you buy and it does not come back. Insurance and registration have their own boxes. For one car.
itemIncludes.carInsuranceStart: The first insurance payment on the car before you drive. You pay it once, then monthly, and it does not come back. For the car.
itemIncludes.carRegistration: Registration, plates and title transfer fees. You pay when you register the car and it does not come back. For the car.
itemIncludes.healthInsuranceStart: The first month's health insurance premium, before the monthly costs start. You pay in the first month and it does not come back. Choose "one person" or "the whole family" above.
itemIncludes.childcareStart: Enrolment and the first payment for daycare, for each child under 5 (our analysis). You pay when you enrol the child and it does not come back. The monthly cost is in the monthly costs.
itemIncludes.otherMoving: Any moving cost that has no box above. You pay in the first month and it does not come back. Type the total for the whole family.
itemIncludes.rent: The month's rent only. You pay it every month and it does not come back. Power and water have their own box. For the whole flat.
itemIncludes.phone: The monthly mobile plan. You pay every month and it does not come back. For the whole family.
itemIncludes.food: Groceries, supermarket and home cooking. An ordinary cost you pay every month and it does not come back. For each person.
itemIncludes.healthInsurance: The monthly health insurance premium once it has started. You pay every month and it does not come back. Choose "one person" or "the whole family" above.
itemIncludes.carInsurance: The monthly car insurance premium. You pay every month and it does not come back. For the car.
itemIncludes.childcare: Daycare every month, for children under 5 (our analysis: the age of kindergarten in the US). You pay every month and it does not come back. For each child.
itemIncludes.otherMonthly: Any monthly cost that has no box above. You pay it every month and it does not come back. Type the total for the whole family.
itemIncludes.familyAbroadMonthly: Rent, food and any cost of the family at home during this time. You pay every month until the family arrives and it does not come back. For the whole family.
itemIncludes.quickPaperwork: Registration, medical, documents and every fee up to the green card. You pay from registration until you travel, and most of it does not come back. Type the total for the whole family.
itemIncludes.quickTravel: Tickets, bags and travel insurance. You pay before you travel, and it usually does not come back. Type the total for the whole family.
itemIncludes.quickHousing: Temporary stay, the rental deposit (it comes back), first rent, furniture and home supplies. You pay in the first month. Type the total for the whole family.
itemIncludes.quickCar: Buying the car, insuring it, registering it and the licence. You pay in the first month and it does not come back. Type the total for the whole family.
itemIncludes.quickMonthly: Rent, utilities, food, transport and health insurance for one month. You pay every month and it does not come back. Type the total for the whole family.
itemIncludes.medicalExamChild: The general examination and vaccinations at the embassy's doctor. You pay the doctor before the interview and it does not come back. For each child under 15. Usually no X-ray or blood test.
itemIncludes.policeCertificate: Getting the police certificate. You pay before the interview and it does not come back. For each person aged 16 or older; younger children do not need one.
itemIncludes.ticket: A flight ticket for each adult (12 or older). You pay before you travel, and it usually does not come back (it depends on the fare). This split is the usual airline pattern (unconfirmed): ask your airline.
itemIncludes.ticketChild: A flight ticket for each child aged 2 to 11. You pay before you travel, and it usually does not come back. Usually cheaper than an adult's (unconfirmed): ask your airline.
itemIncludes.ticketInfant: A flight ticket for each infant under 2. You pay before you travel, and it usually does not come back. Usually a small share of the adult fare (unconfirmed).
itemIncludes.passport: Getting or renewing your own passport. You pay it before registering and it does not come back. For the main applicant only.
itemIncludes.registrationFee: The official fee to register for the lottery. You pay it online when you register. It is per entry: one entry if only you register.
itemIncludes.excessBaggage: Fees for extra weight or extra bags. You pay before you travel or at the airport and it does not come back. For the whole family.
itemIncludes.firstMonthRent: The first month's rent. You pay it before you move in and it does not come back. For the whole flat.
itemIncludes.utilities: The power, water and gas bills. You pay every month and it does not come back. For the whole flat.
itemIncludes.internet: The home internet subscription. You pay every month and it does not come back. For the whole flat.
itemIncludes.transport: Public transport or fuel. You pay every month and it does not come back. For the whole family.
itemIncludes.visaFee: The interview fee (the visa fee). You pay it at the embassy on the interview day if it was not paid before. It does not come back even if the visa is refused. For each applicant.
itemIncludes.immigrantFee: The green card fee (the USCIS fee). You pay it online after the visa is issued and before you travel. It covers processing the file and printing the green card. For each person, children too.
